content.title: Content Engine
content.subtitle: Cedar Ridge is already a listing. This is the desk's weekly seller-side rhythm — same week, same voice.

thinking.t: Topic from the library: when a solo GP should start the transition conversation.
Outline first. Principal approves before a draft exists.
Approved outline → full piece → atomize to LinkedIn, email, newsletter teaser.

content.stream: Most solo owners wait until they're tired. By then the numbers have already started to slip, and buyers can see it. The better window is two to three years out: production still clean, the associate question still open, the building still an option rather than a scramble.

approval.q: Send this outline to the principal before anyone writes the draft?
approval.note: The system absorbs the rhythm. The point of view stays human.

webinar.title: Webinar pack
webinar.subtitle: Same Content Engine. A recorded session becomes clips plus written follow-on — one voice file.

thinking.t: Pick 4 standalone moments: hook, number, story, what to do next.
Cut verticals with captions. Draft YouTube title block and a newsletter from the same transcript.

webinar.stream: Clip 2 hook: "If your collections dipped and you told yourself it was a season, it usually wasn't." Captions on. Newsletter teaser points back to the full session — not a second essay.

approval.q: Principal signs off on the four hooks before anything publishes?
approval.note: Video is the same station as the blog. Not a second product.

radar.title: Seller Origination
radar.subtitle: How the next listing shows up. Public signals, ranked. Sample territory — not a live file.

thinking.t: License-year band + solo flag + review velocity as a proxy for new patients.
A new associate on the masthead is succession already underway — deprioritize, don't mark hot.
Human grades the Verify flags. The job does not decide who you call.

insights.v: Review velocity ≥ 8/mo tracks the $800k+ profile in this vertical.
Successor visible → not a hot listing lead.

approval.q: Keep Cedar Ridge as Call first? No successor on the site, velocity is in band.
approval.note: The list is a suggestion. Who you actually want as a client stays human.

diligence.title: Due Diligence
diligence.subtitle: Cedar Ridge Family Dentistry — sample P&L, tax return, lease. The agent never decides.

thinking.t: Read the source pack. Identify providers. Don't trust the recap sheet yet.
Add-backs only where the document supports them. Flag the rest as questions.
Lease term vs. stated remaining years. Payroll vs. W-2/1099 mix.

insights.v: Owner auto $14.2k — titled to the practice, personal use noted on the schedule. Ask for the title.
Hygiene production down 9% year-over-year with no staffing note. Ask why.
5 years remaining, 3% bumps, no stated assignment clause in the copy we have. Confirm with counsel.
Recap shows lab at $41k; invoices in the pack sum to $47.6k. Don't smooth it.

approval.q: Send the eleven questions to the doctor before anyone writes a valuation?
approval.note: Generate and verify are separate. This pass finds; it does not price.

cim.title: CIM / Listing
cim.subtitle: Numbers already signed off by the broker. Narratives and the listing pack — then a branded PDF.

thinking.t: Trust the verified sheet. Do not re-invent collections, SDE, or asking.
Thesis: clean solo GP, hygiene dip is a lever not a hole — only if the doctor answered it.
Write CIM fields + six marketing assets. Renderer stamps the PDF from the same JSON.

cim.stream: Cedar Ridge is a five-operatory solo general practice with a long-tenured owner and a patient base that still walks in on the name. Trailing collections $1.12M. SDE $385k on the recast the broker already signed. The hygiene dip is in the Q&A: two days uncovered after a retirement, now back to full — a growth lever, not a haircut, if you staff it. Asking is the broker's number. This copy does not invent one.

insights.v: Stable solo GP. Staffing the hygiene block is the first lever.
Asking price, multiples, and what goes to buyers under NDA — broker.

rec.t: Broker reviews the CIM and blurbs before the PDF goes to Drive.
rec.note: The renderer is a stamp. Authorship is the skill. Approval is the product.

escrow.title: Escrow Onboarding
escrow.subtitle: Offer accepted. Same-day kickoff pack — generic TC and escrow, not a named vendor.

thinking.t: Pull parties, prices, EMDs, financing, and contingency math from the signed LOI.
Practice only. Buyer is not taking the building — keep the lease section in the intros.
Four artifacts: portal fields, escrow-open, buyer intro, seller intro. No addresses in the drafts.

approval.q: TC reviews the four drafts, then portal + escrow go out together?
approval.note: Onboarding is the start of the command center. The desk then runs the deal through close.

artifacts.v: Seller–Buyer, practice only, prices, EMD, contingency dates, commission TBD if the listing agreement isn't in the pack.
Draft to the firm's escrow partner. LOI attached. Counsel TBD.
EMD in three business days. Data room after it clears. Lease application in play — they're not buying the building.
Escrow is opening. Lender will ask for more docs. Route the buyer through the TC, not the front desk.
